evidence_class: PRE-REGISTRATION (hypotheses only; no new holdout result or submission slot at registration)
scope: Fault-zone-anatomy lane only. Tested families excluded: host bend/scarp strike (H57-H), two-host relay (H57-I2), slip-sense transition (H57-J), broad candidate-edge orientation, length-width normalization, and prior sense/distance ablations. The first item was previously proposed as H6-1 but had no current-instrument matched holdout test; it is the only hypothesis to be tested in this session.
evidence_limits: The 0.2778 and 0.2708 labels are OWNER-REPORTED from repository evidence, not ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED exact-file receipts.
The current official competition feature TIFF and cached band arrays are absent. The selected geometry-only test does not require them; no geophysical band will be rebuilt or silently substituted.
A local holdout recovers withheld catalogued fault components, not independent newly mapped live faults; positive results would not be live-score forecasts.
ranking_basis: Qualitative expected-value priority combines plausible DTI direction, evidence relevance, implementation cost, and whether required data are locally available. These are not numerical score projections.

validation_plan.withholding: whole catalogue components, label-blind eroded quadrants, 3 px feature-context buffer
validation_plan.catalogue_features: visible faults only; exact unhidden mapped-fault mask at scoring
validation_plan.metric: pooled DTI, alpha=0.2, beta=0.8, 300 m triangular kernel
validation_plan.leakage_canary: max(AUC, 1-AUC) per feature; any value >0.90 stops the hypothesis
validation_plan.intervention: From the same training-only anatomy ranking, prune predictions whose distance to the visible catalogue is <=2 px; compare with an equal-count random prune in each held-out quadrant. The 2 px radius is fixed from the prior file-level audit before this holdout; no threshold sweep.
validation_plan.emission: Training-fold prevalence and training-fold fitted zone only; no test-positive count chooses the budget or locations.
validation_plan.promotion_rule: S7-1 is scientifically retained only if its paired 95% CI lower bound is >0 versus matched-random pruning and it is not weaker than the current comparable holdout best under the same instrument. No competition slot is selected or used.
validation_plan.stop_rule: If the literal full-registry pre-placement uniqueness rule fires, log the duplicate and stop before production-dot placement.

pre_run_gate_audit.input_pins: Bridged fault grid, sample grid, and geometry CSV SHA256 pins verified; runner will recheck before fitting.
pre_run_gate_audit.registry: The 696-raster baseline index is stale for four public main heads; four open PR heads were found but their raster contents were not scanned. The indexed universal-support witness remains in unchanged 17GEMSDOE main, so any nonempty allowed dot set still fails the literal 0.70 overlap gate. No candidate scan or production placement is authorized.

historical_comparator.reason: Evaluator implementation hash mismatch; version string alone does not establish comparability.

pre_run_gate_audit.zone_budget_caveat: A training-positive 90th-percentile zone contains approximately 90% of training positives by construction; this yields about a 10% training-only cap shrink but does not adapt to test-fold support shift.

ranked.hypothesis: At a fixed per-fold dot count, suppressing candidate predictions within 2 px of the visible known-fault catalogue improves DTI more than removing the same number of randomly selected predictions.
layers: visible-only distance/anatomy features and fitted intensity from src/gems57/anatomy.py
ranked.physical_signature: A fitted near-trace exclusion band in the emitted dot allocation; no edge transform and no assumed Riedel angle.
ranked.why_it_might_find_new_faults: The task penalizes dots without nearby new-fault pixels, while the organizer permits new geometry near a known trace. The holdout therefore tests, rather than assumes, whether the closest 200 m of candidate allocation is mostly redundant or still recovers real strands.
ranked.difference_from_implemented: Distance is already an anatomy predictor and scripts/proximal_sweep.py reports a model surrogate, but no current buffered holdout has compared a fixed-radius, equal-count proximal prune against a matched-random prune. This is H6-1 from the previous slate, now testable without the missing geophysical stack.
ranked.expected_gain: Low-to-moderate and highly uncertain; the owner-reported nested-raster change makes the test worth running, but catalogue hide-and-recover may favor close continuations.
ranked.implementation_cost: Low; one shared-model fit per spatial fold plus paired allocations/evaluator calls.
ranked.data_status: Required bridge-grid files are present. No new external data required; official-origin identity remains unverified in this checkout.
ranked.non_fault_mimic: Digitization offsets, trace generalization, and map-resolution mismatch can make a real secondary strand appear close to or far from the catalogue.

ranked.hypothesis: A visible-host slip-rate term, fit jointly with distance, component length, relative orientation and available sense, improves the damage-zone intensity over length alone.
ranked.physical_signature: Cross-validated residual variation in perpendicular distance/strand density by recorded rate after conditioning on visible-host length; the width law and orientation distribution are fit on training folds, not imposed.
ranked.why_it_might_find_new_faults: If present-day rate distinguishes active hosts whose secondary structures are more expressed, it can prioritize unrecorded nearby strands instead of extending every trace equally.
ranked.difference_from_implemented: The current anatomy uses log visible-component length as a noisy displacement proxy; the repository's prior slate described slip-rate scaling but no current buffered holdout or leak-safe rate-to-raster join has been verified.
ranked.expected_gain: Moderate but uncertain; rate is not cumulative displacement and may not explain damage-zone width.
ranked.implementation_cost: Medium-high; host/record matching, units/missingness audit, visible-only join and fold-wise canaries are prerequisites.
ranked.data_status: CSV extracts are present and hash-pinned as local bridge data; joins to rasterized hosts and independent official-origin authentication are unresolved. Not viable until those audits pass.
ranked.non_fault_mimic: Reporting and mapping effort covary with assigned slip rate; a rate association may reflect survey/catalogue completeness rather than fracture damage.

ranked.hypothesis: Explicit visible-network branch order and junction-angle context adds information about secondary-strand concentration beyond distance, local density, host bend and two-host relay features.
layers: visible-only fault network topology derived from the binary trace mask
recorded sense from data/external/trace_segments_utm11.csv only where a visible trace record supports it
ranked.physical_signature: Skeleton-graph node degree, local branch-angle dispersion and junction-distance surfaces, with angular distributions estimated from training-fold withheld segments.
ranked.why_it_might_find_new_faults: Stress interactions around mapped intersections and branch nodes can localize small splays that are missed by a smooth isotropic distance halo.
ranked.difference_from_implemented: Existing density, multi-scale bend and two-host relay features do not encode graph node degree/branch order explicitly; generic bend and relay families are excluded from this hypothesis.
ranked.expected_gain: Small-to-moderate; junctions are localized, and pixel-skeleton topology is sensitive to map rasterization.
ranked.implementation_cost: Medium; skeleton stability tests, visible-only graph construction, per-feature canaries and spatially blocked ablation required.
ranked.data_status: Uses present bridge geometry; no new external data required. Official raster provenance remains the bridge limitation.
ranked.non_fault_mimic: Rasterization corners, digitization vertices and map joins can create artificial graph nodes.

ranked.hypothesis: Within the already fitted fault-zone support, a radiometric K/eTh alteration contrast modifies strand intensity in relay/damage corridors.
layers: Official USGS GeoDAWN airborne radiometric potassium (K) and equivalent thorium (eTh) grids
visible-only fault-zone geometry and recorded sense where available
ranked.physical_signature: Multiscale K/eTh contrast or robust local edge relative to the nearest visible host, evaluated only inside a zone fitted from training-fold holdouts.
ranked.why_it_might_find_new_faults: Fault-hosted fluid circulation may alter potassium relative to relatively immobile thorium and expose concealed secondary structures; an alteration contrast is corroborating evidence, not proof of a fault.
ranked.difference_from_implemented: The current H57-H experiment used detrended elevation and existing H57 work tested magnetic-edge orientation; this is a radiometric ratio, spatially restricted to the fault-anatomy lane, not an unrestricted whole-footprint detector.
ranked.expected_gain: Potentially moderate, but too uncertain to rank as an actionable model without raster overlap and leakage testing.
ranked.implementation_cost: High; official binary retrieval, licensing/metadata audit, CRS/coverage registration, derived-band validation and a new holdout run.
ranked.data_status: BLOCKED / NOT VIABLE NOW. Official catalogue record: https://www.usgs.gov/data/geodawn-airborne-magnetic-and-radiometric-surveys-northwestern-great-basin-nevada-and (ScienceBase DOI 10.5066/P93LGLVQ). The current sandbox has no official K/eTh raster; coverage, downloadability, grid overlap and license of a specific file were not verified. The competition feature page https://www.drivendata.org/competitions/306/competition-doe-gems/data/ is login-gated in the saved audit; its 19-band bridge stack is also absent.
ranked.non_fault_mimic: Lithologic potassium variation, weathering and radiometric flight-line/terrain-clearance artifacts can mimic alteration near structures.

post_run_cross_branch_audit.evidence_class: POST-RUN PROVENANCE / NOVELTY CORRECTION; original preregistration retained
post_run_cross_branch_audit.correction: The branch-local pre-run inventory did not fetch its own origin/main. H6-1, the same conceptual 2-px proximity-prune versus equal-count random test on the retained E2 allocator, was already merged before the S7-1 run. The initial scope claim that no such current-instrument matched test existed was therefore incomplete. S7-1 used a different base allocator, but is not a novel hypothesis or independent holdout.
post_run_cross_branch_audit.action: Preserve the original pre-registration and S7-1 receipt as historical records; no score was recomputed, no experiment was repeated, no result was pooled, and no candidate was promoted.

current_comparable_best_found_after_main.interpretation: The current evaluator/split best was already available in main before S7-1 but was missed by the stale branch. S7-1 is pointwise below it; no paired cross-model significance calculation was performed.
